title: Interface-induced spin-resolved type-II band alignment and enhanced magnetic anisotropy in MSe2/WTe2 (M = V, Cr, Mn, Fe and Co) van der Waals heterobilayers
authors: Paras Poswal, Ranjit Pati, Neeraj Shukla
abstract: Two-dimensional van der Waals heterobilayers provide an attractive platform for the development of next-generation spintronic devices. Here, first-principles calculations are performed to investigate the structural, electronic and magnetic properties of MSe2/WTe2 (M = V, Cr, Mn, Fe, and Co) van der Waals heterobilayers. The pristine WSe2/WTe2 heterobilayer in AA'-configuration is found to be energetically favorable and exhibits type-II band alignment with a band gap of 0.70 eV, and this provides an ideal platform for controlling carrier transport. Substituting W with 3d transition metal atoms, induces long-range magnetic ordering and reconstructs the spin-resolved electronic band structure. The formation of the heterointerface generates pronounced charge redistribution and an intrinsic built-in electric field, leading to interface-induced electronic reconstruction. MnSe2/WTe2 heterobilayer exhibits half-metallicity, whereas FeSe2/WTe2 heterobilayer simultaneously exhibits half-metallicity and spin-resolved type-II band alignment. Interfacial electronic reconstruction further produces a substantial perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, driving MnSe2 from an in-plane easy axis with MAE value of 1.10 meV in the isolated monolayer to a robust out-of-plane easy axis with MAE value of 20.8 meV in the heterobilayer. Among all the structures, CoSe2/WTe2 heterobilayer exhibits maximum Curie temperature (273.87 K). The combined results establish that interface engineering makes MSe2/WTe2 heterobilayers as a promising candidates for next-generation low-dimensional spintronic applications.
summary: This work theoretically investigates $	ext{MSe}_2/	ext{WTe}_2$ van der Waals heterobilayers to engineer next-generation spintronic materials. By substituting W with various 3d metals, the researchers demonstrate that interface formation induces favorable type-II band alignment and dramatically enhances perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. The findings establish these heterostructures as promising candidates for low-dimensional electronic and magnetic devices.
main_problem: The study investigates how interface engineering in van der Waals heterobilayers can enhance electronic properties, specifically achieving spin-resolved type-II band alignment and robust perpendicular magnetic anisotropy for spintronic applications.
main_result: The $	ext{MSe}_2/	ext{WTe}_2$ heterobilayers exhibit significant improvements upon interface formation, with $	ext{FeSe}_2/	ext{WTe}_2$ showing simultaneous half-metallicity, type-II alignment, and enhanced magnetic anisotropy.
method: The research employs first-principles Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, supplemented by methods to calculate Magnetic Anisotropy Energy (MAE) and model finite-temperature magnetism using Monte Carlo simulations.
model_or_system: The physical system is the $	ext{MSe}_2/	ext{WTe}_2$ van der Waals heterobilayer, where M is a 3d transition metal ($	ext{V}, 	ext{Cr}, 	ext{Mn}, 	ext{Fe}, 	ext{Co}$). The analysis focuses on structural stability, electronic band structure, and magnetic coupling across the heterointerface.
key_observables: Type-II band gap (e.g., 0.70 eV), half-metallicity, Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy Energy (MAE), Curie Temperature ($T_C$), and built-in electric fields.
important_parameters: The study compares various transition metals (V to Co) and stacking configurations ($	ext{AA}'$ preferred). Key energy scales include MAE values (e.g., $20.8 	ext{ meV}$ for $	ext{MnSe}_2$).
main_assumptions: Calculations rely on DFT approximations (GGA+U), and magnetic behavior at finite temperatures is modeled using classical Heisenberg Hamiltonians.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate stacking sequences, band structures showing type-II alignment, charge density redistribution profiles indicating built-in fields, and angular dependence of MAE.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the structural stability, electronic properties (band alignment/charge transfer), and magnetic anisotropy enhancement across different $	ext{M}$ substitutions in the heterobilayer system.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism and electronics, the detailed theoretical modeling of interfacial coupling mechanisms—which dictate emergent quantum phenomena like spin-selectivity and enhanced anisotropy—is highly relevant to understanding engineered quantum interfaces.
